title: I built a SaaS, then open-sourced it instead. Retrogaze: hardware-legal pixel art for 7 retro systems, MIT license.
author: lerugray
selftext:
A while back I posted here about Retrogaze when it was a paid web service I was trying to run as a small SaaS. Since then a couple of my other projects took off, so I made a decision: I open-sourced the whole thing under MIT. It's free, it's yours, fork it and ship something with it.

Repo: https://github.com/lerugray/retrogaze

What it does:

- It generates sprites and tilesets inside the actual hardware limits of the NES, SNES, Genesis / Mega Drive, Game Boy (DMG, Pocket and Color), Commodore 64 and PC Engine. Real palettes, per-tile color caps, real grids.
- The constraint engine also works on art you already have, generated or hand-drawn. Give it a PNG and it returns the image inside the system's limits, with a JSON report of what changed. The engine and the CLI run fully offline and need no key.
- Image generation runs on fal.ai with your own key. I am not paying for your generations and there is no account, no signup, no hosted tier anymore.
- It comes three ways: a web app you run locally, a CLI, and an MCP server that works with pixel-mcp and Aseprite.

Some examples from the old site:


https://i.redd.it/qs7cijprxqzh1.png

https://i.redd.it/4ys8e2otxqzh1.png

https://i.redd.it/z6x4lc3vxqzh1.png

https://i.redd.it/66nhwalwxqzh1.gif

The part I am proudest of is code mode. Instead of an image model, art is drawn from a small program in the pxl DSL. The build then proves the art is legal on real hardware rules (on NES: the 2C02 palette, attribute areas, 3 colors per sprite, 8 sprites per scanline, pattern-table budgets; SNES BG mode 1 rules are in there too) and exports the actual bytes the console loads: CHR, palettes, nametables, OAM, plus ca65/cc65 includes. There is a proof harness that runs the exported bytes in Mesen 2. Every violation names the source line that painted the bad pixels.

Full disclosure since the repo shows it anyway: the code still contains leftovers from the hosted product (Supabase auth, LemonSqueezy payments, email). They do nothing unless you configure them, and the README says exactly which files they are. Run the engine, CLI, web app and MCP server without any of it.

I am a game designer, not a company, and I would rather see this used than sit on it. Bug reports and forks welcome. If you make something with it, I want to see it.
